messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] P95 control-plane 5xx rate > 4% for 3m (auth/org-lookup/billing). Pager sent to #incidents and @sre-oncall. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CP/ctrlplane-errors?from=now-15m&to=now
Alex Kim: I’m on it — picking up pager. Observed spike at 10:12 UTC, errors mostly 502/504 and timeout in front of org-lookup service.
Priya Patel: Confirming — customer reports coming in via Zendesk. Primary error signature: "UpstreamServiceError: org-lookup timed out (deadline)".
Jae Park: I’m seeing similar on controlplane-gateway logs: lots of `503 upstream connect error or disconnect` with grpc status 14.
Nina Lopez: Quick heads-up — some high-volume customers on Dedicated might see degraded auth checks causing login failures. Not yet widespread but could cascade.
Alex Kim: Triage plan: 1) Identify if this is a single dependency or multiple. 2) Mitigate with temporary fallback for org-lookup via cached index. 3) Add rate-limiter/batching at gateway. 4) If necessary, roll traffic to passive region.
Priya Patel: Running quick query on traces for trace_id samples. Example trace: `trace/abc123` shows 2.1s wait to org-lookup, then 5xx returned.
Jae Park: K/V: `kubectl -n controlplane logs -l app=controlplane-gateway | grep "org-lookup" | tail -n 50` output:
```
E0314 10:13:05.123 gateway.go:412] upstream request failed: Post "http://org-lookup.svc.cluster.local/lookup": context deadline exceeded
E0314 10:13:05.125 gateway.go:418] returning 502 to client, correlation_id=xyz-321
```
Nina Lopez: Also seeing billing service returning `500 internal` with stack `billing.LookupAccount -> sql: database is overloaded` — might be DB hotspots.
Alex Kim: So auth and org-lookup and billing are all showing failures. Looks like a shared downstream dependency or sudden load spike causing cascading timeouts. Hypothesis: recent config rollout to org-lookup increased CPU or introduced blocking sync. Check recent deploys.
Priya Patel: Checking deploy bot: `deploy-bot reported: org-lookup v2.14 deployed to prod at 09:58 UTC by infra-cd`.
Jae Park: Rolling back org-lookup v2.14 to v2.13 could be fastest mitigant. But before rollback, can we toggle read-only cache mode? There’s a feature-flag `org_lookup_cache_read_only` we can enable via config-service.
Alex Kim: Good call. While Priya prepares rollback, I’ll enable cache read-only.
Priya Patel: Enabling via config API: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://config.redwood.internal/api/flags/org_lookup_cache_read_only -d '{"enabled":true}'` — returned 200.
Jae Park: After flag flip, error rate dropped from 4.2% -> 2.1% in 2 minutes. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CP/ctrlplane-errors?from=now-10m&to=now
Nina Lopez: Customer impact list (derived from spikes in auth failures):
- AcmeCorp (high) — login and job submissions failing intermittently
- BrightApps (medium) — API call retries increased, timeouts on start-up
- Multiple self-serve customers (low) — increased latency but functioning

Alex Kim: Good. Keep cache read-only as temporary mitigation. Priya, proceed with rollback plan to fully restore. Coordinate with infra-cd.
Priya Patel: Initiating rollback: `infra-cd rollback org-lookup --to v2.13 --namespace=prod` — started 10:19 UTC. Keeping monitoring.
incidents-bot: @channel Incident status changed: Mitigating — partial mitigation via cache read-only and rollback in progress.
Jae Park: Observability note: KV cache hit rate improved after flag flip; backend DB CPU for billing still elevated. I’ll open a short-term DB connection cap on billing to reduce overload: `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 200;` (ops-applied)
Nina Lopez: Applying lightweight throttling policy at controlplane-gateway for non-critical endpoints to reduce pressure: `gateway-rate-limit: /v1/metrics -> 20rps` applied.
Alex Kim: After rollback finished at 10:22 UTC, we saw error rate drop to 0.6% within 4 minutes. Rolling windows look healthy.
Priya Patel: Confirmed: rollback to v2.13 completed, org-lookup pods at ready=3/3. Logs show no deadline exceeded messages.
Jae Park: Billing DB CPU trending down after connection cap and throttling. 5xx now under SLO threshold.
incidents-bot: Incident status changed: Resolved (partial) — customer-facing errors reduced; ongoing monitoring.
Nina Lopez: Next steps: 1) Postmortem owner? 2) Investigate v2.14 changeset for blocking calls and DB usage. 3) Add more robust canary checks pre-deploy for org-lookup (DB query latency guard). 4) Run customer-impact reconciliation.
Alex Kim: I’ll own the postmortem. Priya will help with deployment checks. Jae will investigate DB hotspots. Nina will coordinate customer comms and Zendesk triage.
Priya Patel: Adding follow-ups in backlog: `INC-2213 investigate-org-lookup-v214`, `INC-2214 add-canary-db-latency-gate`, `INC-2215 improve-cache-fallback`
Jae Park: Handoff: I need to head off for another meeting, handing oncall to @sre-oncall for continued monitoring for 2h. Key things to watch: error% > 1.5% for 5m, billing DB CPU > 70%, org-lookup pod restarts.
Alex Kim: Acknowledged. @sre-oncall take it.
sre-oncall: Taking over monitoring. I’ll post updates every 15m or on change. Thanks team.
incidents-bot: Incident closed for pager escalation. Please create postmortem in #postmortems and tag `sev-2`.
Alex Kim: Quick note for postmortem: timeline, config flip, rollback, DB throttle, customer impact, tickets created. Will include reproducer from v2.14 in staging.
Priya Patel: Zendesk summary draft: "We experienced elevated errors affecting login and API requests between 10:12-10:28 UTC due to a faulty org-lookup deploy. We applied a cache fallback and rolled back the release; affected customers should be back to normal. We will follow up with detailed RCA and remediation timeline."
Nina Lopez: Posting update to status.redwood.com after postmortem published.
Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. Closing thread for now — monitoring continues.
